text: Applying for a US IPO with just $10 is almost impossible – most IPOs require a minimum allotment of $5,000 to $10,000 and the allotment is usually a fraction of that. Even if you somehow got a share, you’d still face the hidden spread cost of the broker’s order‑flow revenue, plus the 0.01‑0.02% bid‑ask spread on the first trade. For Reliance on Zerodha, the delivery‑mode charges are: brokerage 0.0%, STT 0.1% of the trade value, SEBI 0.00002%, exchange transaction 0.00059%, stamp duty 0.0015%, GST 0.0011% and a DP charge of ₹15.93. On a ₹10,000 purchase that totals roughly ₹38.15 (0.38% of the trade). If you hold for less than a year you’ll pay 20% short‑term capital‑gain tax on the profit. For cars and battery makers, look at Maruti Suzuki (MTR), Tata Motors (TATAMOTORS.NS), Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and battery names like Exide Industries (EXIDEIND.NS) or Amara Raja (AMARAJAAUTO.NS). Those are the biggest names in the sector you can buy fractionally in the US or whole shares in India.

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: The Leela's spotlight data shows a hotel operator with a -17% revenue drop last quarter and a 46% earnings miss, yet the stock is at all-time highs on 18 buy ratings — that's a classic crowded trade with deteriorating fundamentals. Beta of 0.66 and low 0.26 correlation to Nifty means it hasn't been tested in a real market downdraft; the max drawdown of only -16% over 1.3 years is a small sample. For your Rs 10k budget, the 0.38% round-trip cost plus 20% STCG tax means you need >24% gross just to break even after tax on a short hold. Cars and batteries: Maruti (MARUTI.NS ~Rs 12k) and Exide (EXIDEIND.NS ~Rs 400) fit the budget, but Tata Motors (TATAMOTORS.NS ~Rs 900) and Amara Raja (AMARAJAAUTO.NS ~Rs 1,100) are cheaper entry points. US IPOs with $10? Not happening — minimums are thousands and fractional IPO allotments don't exist.
